Create and immediately send a new email in Outlook to the specified recipients.

Returns the sent message's ``message_id`` and ``conversation_id`` so callers

having to search Sent Items.

The confirmation message names how many recipient addresses the email went to
across To, Cc and Bcc.

parameters.name: body

parameters.name: to_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the recipients of the email

parameters.name: cc_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the CC recipients of the email.

parameters.name: bcc_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the BCC recipients of the email.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The content type of the email body. Defaults to plain text.

tools.name: CreateDraftReply
tools.description:
Create a reply or reply-all draft for an existing Outlook email without sending it.

The draft is threaded to the original message and saved to the Drafts folder,
so it can be reviewed, edited, and sent later. For a reply-all, the original
recipients (excluding the mailbox owner) are populated automatically. Use
cc_add to copy someone in on the draft, including someone who was never on
the thread, and cc_remove to take somebody off the copied line; who the
reply is addressed to is the thread's own and reply_type decides it. This
tool never sends the email.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email to create a reply draft for

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the reply draft

parameters.name: reply_type
parameters.description: Specify ReplyType.REPLY to draft a reply to only the sender, or ReplyType.REPLY_ALL to draft a reply to all recipients. Defaults to ReplyType.REPLY.

parameters.name: cc_add
parameters.description: Addresses to copy on the reply draft, in addition to whoever Outlook already copied. On a reply to all recipients Outlook copies the thread's other participants, and they stay copied — this only adds. Omit it to copy nobody new. Each address is copied once, and an address the draft already addresses is left addressed rather than also copied, so nobody receives the reply twice.

parameters.name: cc_remove
parameters.description: Addresses to take off the reply draft's copied line. Anyone Outlook copied and this does not name stays copied. Omit it to remove nobody; an address that is not on the copied line is ignored. An address the draft addresses cannot be taken off it — reply_type decides that line — so naming one is refused and no draft is kept.

parameters.name: bcc
parameters.description: Addresses to blind-copy on the reply draft. This does not remove an address from To or Cc: it remains visible to other recipients if it is also on either line, including through cc_add. To move someone from Cc to Bcc, include them in cc_remove and bcc, not cc_add; an address on To cannot be hidden through bcc. Outlook never blind-copies anyone on a reply, so this is the whole line rather than a change to one. Omit it to blind-copy nobody.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: How body is read. Plain text reaches the recipient as the characters supplied, line breaks and angle brackets included; html reads body as markup, so tags in it render instead of being shown. Defaults to plain text. A reply draft is always stored as an HTML document because the quoted original is one, so this decides how body is read rather than what is stored.

output.description: The created draft. message_id is the draft's own id, not the id of the message being replied to.

body.value: Thank you for reaching out. I've reviewed the details and will get back to you with a full response by end of week.

tools.name: CreateMailFolder
tools.description:
Create a mail folder in the user's own Outlook mailbox, to keep related messages together.

The folder is created in the signed-in user's own mailbox, and in no other:
this tool cannot reach a mailbox named by address, whether a team mailbox or
another person's.
Safe to call for a folder that may already exist: an existing folder of the
same name under the same parent is returned instead of a duplicate. A
parent_folder that names no folder in the mailbox creates nothing.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name for the new folder, as it should read in Outlook. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the trimmed name is what gets created.

parameters.name: parent_folder
parameters.description: The folder to create this one inside, given as the word inbox or archive, or as a folder_id taken from a mail-folder listing of this mailbox. A display name or a path is refused: one display name can belong to several folders, and proving which one was meant costs a read of every folder in the mailbox, so the parent is named exactly or the request is declined. When omitted, the folder is created at the top level of the mailbox.

output.description: The folder with the message counts that belong to it, the folder that holds it, and whether this call is what created it.

tools.name: GetEmail
tools.description:
Retrieve a single email message by its ID.

Returns email metadata and body content. By default, the body is returned
as plain text (HTML tags stripped) and capped at 5000 characters. Set
body_format to HTML to get the original markup. Use body_offset to
continue reading long emails: body_total_characters reports how long
the body is, and body_next_offset is where the next call resumes.

Use this tool to read the full content of an email whose ID is already
known, and to page through a body too long for one response.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email message to retrieve.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: Format for the returned email body. PLAIN_TEXT strips HTML tags for clean reading. HTML returns the original markup. Defaults to PLAIN_TEXT.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Maximum number of characters to return from the email body. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the message without its body. The response always reports body_total_characters, so a body longer than the cap is read by calling again with body_offset set to the returned body_next_offset until body_has_more is false.

parameters.name: body_offset
parameters.description: Character offset to start reading the body from. Use this to continue reading a long email body that was capped by ``max_body_characters`` on a prior call. Defaults to 0 (start of body).

output.description: One page of the message body. body_next_offset is 0 when no further chunk exists, otherwise pass it back to read on. received_date_time_local and sent_date_time_local are always present, with empty strings when the mailbox has no timezone.

tools.name: ListEmailAttachments
tools.description:
List attachment metadata for an email message.

Returns metadata only (name, size, type, etc.). Attachment content is not included.
Use this tool when the user wants to know what files are attached to an email.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email message to list attachments for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of attachments to return. Max is 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed position to start from. Repeat the same arguments alongside it: every page is described by the call that asked for it, so a filter left out on the second page widens the second page. Defaults to 0 (the first result). Pass back the next_offset the response returns rather than adding limit yourself.

output.description: Attachment metadata without the file bytes. has_next_page is false when no further page exists; while it is true, pass back next_offset to read on.

tools.name: ListEmails
tools.description:
List email messages in the user's mailbox.

Returns ordinary mail by default: Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and
Drafts are left out unless named in folders, folder_ids or conversation_id.

Rows carry a 255-character body preview unless include_body is set, which
returns each message in full up to max_body_characters.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Well-known folders to list mail from. Omit to read every folder except Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and Drafts. Naming folders replaces that default rather than adding to it, so pass deleteditems to read deleted mail. Combined with conversation_id, this narrows the thread to these folders. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: folder_ids
parameters.description: Ids of user-created folders to list mail from. Combined with any value given for folders. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Return only messages in this conversation, across every folder including Sent Items and Deleted Items. Use it to read a whole thread. Naming folders or folder_ids alongside it narrows the thread to those folders, so leave both out to see all of it. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject match, as a value plus the operator to compare it with. Defaults to None (no subject filter).

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Sender email address match, as a value plus the operator to compare it with. Defaults to None (no sender filter).

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: True for read mail, False for unread. Defaults to None (both).

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: True for mail carrying attachments, False for mail without. Defaults to None (both).

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Return only mail at this importance level, and nothing else. Never use it to express an exclusion: setting it to normal to mean 'not low' drops every high-importance message. Use exclude_importance for that. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: exclude_importance
parameters.description: Return mail at every importance level except this one. Leave importance out alongside it: naming both narrows to a single level instead of excluding one. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: flag_status
parameters.description: Return only mail in this follow-up flag state. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Omit it, or leave it empty, for no lower bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). The whole of that day is included. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no upper bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused, using Outlook's Focused Inbox split. Sender addresses are not inspected. Mailboxes with Focused Inbox turned off classify everything as focused, so this filters nothing there. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Property to sort results by. Defaults to received date.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of messages to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same listing arguments alongside it: a cursor names a listing rather than a row number, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. Defaults to None (the first page).

output.description: One page of the matching messages. cursor is an empty string when this listing will serve no further page, and excluded_folders names what was left out of it.

tools.name: ListMailFolders
tools.description:
List mail folders in the user's mailbox.

Returns folder names, IDs, unread counts, and total item counts. A returned
folder ID is what scopes a mail listing to a user-created folder.
Omit parent_folder_id to list top-level folders, or provide a folder ID
to list its child folders.

parameters.name: parent_folder_id
parameters.description: ID of a parent folder to list child folders of. When omitted, lists top-level mailbox folders.

parameters.name: include_hidden
parameters.description: Whether to include hidden folders in the response. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of folders to return. Max is 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed position to start from. Repeat the same arguments alongside it: every page is described by the call that asked for it, so a filter left out on the second page widens the second page. Defaults to 0 (the first result). Pass back the next_offset the response returns rather than adding limit yourself.

output.description: One page of folders. sub_folders reports whether a folder has children and how many, without listing them.

tools.name: MarkEmails
tools.description:
Set the read state or the follow-up flag on a selection of emails in the user's own mailbox.

One call for a list of ids, a whole thread, or a search, reporting one
outcome per email. Select exactly one way. An email already in the state
asked for is a success that changed nothing, and a job needing more than 50
changes is refused whole rather than part-done.

A request to star, pin, flag or follow up on mail is this call; it never
moves the mail.

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Whether the selected emails should end up read. Defaults to None (leave it as it is).

parameters.name: flag_status
parameters.description: What the follow-up flag should end up as. complete drops the start and due dates, which each row hands back. Defaults to None (leave it as it is); naming start_date or due_date alone sets flagged.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: When the follow-up begins: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS ending in Z or +HH:MM. A bare date means 08:00, and a time with no Z or offset is read, in the mailbox's timezone. Defaults to None (keep the current start; a new deadline with no start begins today).

parameters.name: due_date
parameters.description: The follow-up deadline, in the same formats as start_date. A bare date means 17:00. Records a deadline, not a reminder. Defaults to None (keep the current deadline).

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Narrow to emails currently in these folders: the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or a folder_id from a folder listing. Display names and paths are refused. A word also reaches whatever is filed under that folder. Naming folders replaces the selection's own scope, so name every folder to cover, including sentitems or drafts. Alongside message_ids, an email outside them comes back skipped. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: message_ids
parameters.description: The emails to act on, as the ids a listing, a search or an email read reported. At most 50 per request. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to select emails by, in Outlook's own search syntax, such as from:sara@contoso.com or wording from the subject. Write a phrase as the words alone. Deleted and junk mail are left out unless folders names them. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The thread to act on, as the conversation_id a listing or a search reported. Covers its mail wherever it sits; the user's own sent replies and unsent drafts come back skipped unless folders names them. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Take the next set of a selection a previous call stopped short of, as the cursor it reported. Keep calling with the last cursor, beside the same selector and folders, until it comes back empty. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Report what the request would affect and change nothing, listing the ids, so a job too big for one call can be run in batches of them. Defaults to False.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: MoveEmails
tools.description:
Move a selection of emails into one folder in the user's own mailbox.

Use this single call for a pile of emails instead of moving them one at a
time: it takes a list of ids, a whole conversation, or a search, and reports
one outcome per email.

Select the emails exactly one way. Naming none, or naming two, is refused
and moves nothing, as is a selection of more than 50 emails.

A conversation spans folders, so filing a thread moves the unsent drafts
and sent replies in it too unless folders narrows the selection. Run the
request with count_only first when that matters: it reports which folders
the mail would leave before anything moves.

Anything the caller got wrong -- the selection, an id, a folder that names
several folders or none -- is refused before the first email moves. After
that, an email Outlook refuses is reported as a failed row beside the ones
that moved rather than failing the whole request.

Filing into junk is not a reversible hide: Outlook permanently deletes mail
left in the Junk Email folder after 14 days, it does not report the sender
to Microsoft, and it does not train the junk filter. Tell the user that
before junking mail on their behalf.

Outlook does not record where an email came from, so putting mail back is a
move to the inbox like any other: name inbox as the destination, and name
the folder it is coming out of in folders so mail sitting elsewhere is left
alone.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: The folder to move the selected emails into, as one of the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or as a folder_id from a folder listing of this mailbox. A display name or a path is refused: one display name can belong to several folders, and filing mail into the wrong one is not undoable, so the folder is named exactly or the request is declined. archive is this mailbox's own Archive folder, which is Outlook's One-Click Archive, not a separate Exchange Online archive mailbox. This never creates a folder.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Only move emails that are currently in these folders, each given as one of the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or as a folder_id from a folder listing of this mailbox. Display names and paths are refused, for the same reason as destination. One of the four words also reaches whatever is filed underneath that folder; a folder_id means that folder alone, so to include what is filed underneath one, list its children and name them here too. Use it to file the part of a thread that is in the Inbox without moving the unsent drafts and sent replies in the same thread, and to put junked or deleted mail back in the inbox without disturbing mail that is already elsewhere. Alongside message_ids an email outside these folders is reported as skipped and left where it is; alongside query or conversation_id it is left out of the selection. Naming folders replaces the default exclusion of deleted and junk mail rather than adding to it, and costs one search per folder named. Defaults to None (the whole selection, wherever it sits).

parameters.name: message_ids
parameters.description: The emails to act on, as the ids a listing, a search or a message read reported. At most 50 per request, and more than that is refused rather than trimmed. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to select emails by, in Outlook's own search syntax, such as from:sara@contoso.com or wording from the subject. Write a phrase as the words alone: double quotes around it are refused rather than searched for. Deleted and junk mail are left out unless folders names one of them. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The conversation to act on, as the conversation_id a listing, a search or a message read reported. Selects every message in that thread, including ones in other folders such as unsent drafts and sent replies; name folders alongside it to act on only part of the thread. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Report what the request would affect and change nothing: how many emails would move, which folders they would leave, and their ids. A search or a conversation holding more emails than one request moves is counted rather than refused, so a job too big to run in one call can be sized and then run in batches of those ids. Defaults to False (carry the request out).

output.description:
What one filing request selected, what it changed, and what it did not.

    items holds one row per selected message and is never paginated or
    truncated: the selection cap is the page. It is empty when count_only was
    set, because nothing was written to report. Each row's message_id is an id
    this mailbox accepts for that message, so a row can be chained straight
    into a read or a further move - with one limit named by id_shape: a legacy
    id, which is what a keyword search reports, stops resolving once the
    message has been filed somewhere else, so chain it before the next move
    rather than after. Every row also carries durable_message_id, which names
    the same message after this move whatever shape the selection was made
    with, and is the id to chain when the move has already happened.

    counts covers every row status. succeeded means the message was somewhere
    else and is now in the destination; already_there means it was there
    before this call and is a success rather than a change; skipped means the
    message was outside the folders the caller confined the move to, and it
    was left where it is; throttled means Outlook rate-limited
    that message and nothing was written for it; failed means Outlook refused
    it; not_attempted means the request ran out of time before reaching it;
    indeterminate means Outlook did not say, so read the message before
    retrying.

    complete is true only when every row is succeeded or already_there, and
    true on a count, which leaves nothing undone because it attempts nothing.

    preview is filled only when count_only was set. would_change counts the
    messages that would move, already_there those that are in the destination
    already, not_eligible those outside the folders the move was confined to,
    and classification_unknown those whose current folder could not be read. A
    count describes a selection the move itself would refuse for being over
    the cap rather than refusing to describe it, and says so in notes; the ids
    it would act on ride selection.message_ids so that refusal can be answered
    by moving them in cap-sized batches.

    moved_from aggregates the folders mail left, one entry per source folder. A
    count reports what would leave each folder, so a selection spanning Drafts
    or Sent Items is visible before anything moves.

    selection describes how the messages were chosen. mode is which selector
    was used - message_ids, conversation_id or query - and value is the
    conversation id or the search it was given, empty for a list of ids.
    count_is_exact is false
    when the number is a floor rather than a total, which is what a keyword
    search can honestly report; search_exhaustive says whether the scan reached
    the end of the matches; folders_searched names the folders the selection
    was narrowed to; folders_excluded names the folders a mailbox-wide keyword
    selection left out; duplicates_removed counts ids that named the same
    message twice and were acted on once.

    notes carries consequences of the move that the ledger does not show, such
    as what filing mail into the Junk Email folder does and does not do. They
    follow the folders the mail lands in and leaves, so reaching Junk Email by
    its display name carries the same warnings the junk shorthand does.

tools.name: SaveDraftEmail
tools.description:
Save an email draft in Outlook, creating a new one or revising one that exists.

Supplying message_id revises that draft; omitting it creates a new one. Only the
fields supplied are written — anything left out keeps whatever the draft already
had. Nothing is ever sent.

Returns a DraftMessage. Its message_id identifies the saved draft and can be passed
straight back to this tool to make further changes to it.

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The draft to save the changes onto. Omit it to create a new draft instead. Any un-sent message works, including a reply or forward draft. The id of a draft saved earlier in this conversation is the message_id this tool returned; the id of a draft that already existed comes from listing the Drafts folder.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The subject to set. Omit it to leave the current subject unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body to set. Omit it to leave the current body unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.

parameters.name: to_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of To recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the To line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every To recipient.

parameters.name: cc_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of Cc recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the Cc line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every Cc recipient.

parameters.name: bcc_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of Bcc recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the Bcc line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every Bcc recipient.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The content type of body. Has no effect unless body is supplied. Omit it to keep whatever content type the draft already carries when revising one, or to write plain text on a new draft.

tools.name: SearchEmails
tools.description:
Search emails across the user's entire mailbox.

Combines full-text keyword search with structured filters for sender,
read status, attachments, importance, and more. All provided parameters
are combined with AND.

At least one search criterion is required. folder, only_focused,
include_body and limit narrow or page a result set rather than build one,
so they are not enough on their own.

Junk Email and Deleted Items are left out unless `folder` names one of them;
sent mail and drafts stay searchable. Rows carry a 255-character body preview
unless include_body is set.

Results come back in the search index's own order and cannot be re-sorted.

Outlook's search index answers one query with at most 1,000 messages, so a
walk that runs out of pages has reached the end of what the index serves
rather than the end of the mailbox. The folders left out and the Focused
split are applied to those 1,000 after they are chosen, so a broad term
matching a lot of junk can come back with few rows, or none, while matching
mail exists. A narrower term reaches it; a smaller limit does not.

Use this tool when the user wants to find emails by content, topic, sender,
or a combination of criteria.

.. note::
   Microsoft Graph's ``$search`` on messages is backed by the Microsoft
   Search index, which returns message IDs in the legacy REST-ID format
   even when the client opts into Immutable IDs. Do not directly compare
   these message IDs with Immutable IDs; the formats differ. Use
   ``conversation_id`` to correlate conversations across result sets.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: Words or phrases to search for across email subject, body, and sender fields. All terms must match (AND operator). Defaults to None.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Narrow the hunt to the subject line. Matched as words within the subject rather than as the whole line. Defaults to None (no subject narrowing).

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Filter by sender email address, display name, or alias. When multiple values are provided, emails from any of the senders are returned (OR operator). Defaults to None.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Filter by To-recipient email address or display name. When multiple values are provided, emails to any of the recipients are returned (OR operator). Defaults to None.

parameters.name: attachment_name
parameters.description: Filter by attachment filename. When multiple values are provided, emails with any of the attachment names are returned (OR operator). Defaults to None.

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: Filter for emails with or without attachments. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Filter by email importance level. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Filter by read status. True for read emails, False for unread. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by email category name. Categories are user-defined. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Filter for emails received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no lower bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Filter for emails received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no upper bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Search a single folder instead of the whole mailbox. Omit to search everywhere except Junk Email and Deleted Items; naming a folder replaces that default, so pass deleteditems to search deleted mail. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused, using Outlook's Focused Inbox split. Sender addresses are not inspected. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same search arguments alongside it, only_focused included: a cursor names a search rather than a position in a result set, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. Defaults to None (the first page).

output.description: One page of matches, bodies capped for skimming. cursor is an empty string when this search will serve no further page, and query echoes the search that produced the page -- a cursor handed back beside different arguments is refused rather than continued.

Check which provided mailboxes are reachable via shared mailbox APIs.

This is a capability checker, not an Exchange permission inventory. It
verifies whether each provided mailbox can be reached through a cheap,
read-only Graph call. When checking multiple mailboxes, pass them together
in one ``owner_emails`` list so results can be deduplicated and rate-limited
consistently. Microsoft Graph does not expose exact ``Send As`` vs ``Send
on behalf`` permissions, so the response names that limitation explicitly
instead of guessing.

parameters.description: Mailbox addresses to check. Use exact email addresses or UPNs. Pass all candidate mailboxes in this single list instead of calling the tool once per mailbox. This tool performs read-only Graph probes and returns one result per address.

Create and immediately send an email from a shared or delegated mailbox.

Use this when the user wants the email to be sent from a team inbox (like
sales@ or support@) or from an executive's mailbox they have been
delegated access to, rather than from their own address.

The confirmation message names how many recipient addresses the email went to
across To, Cc and Bcc.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to send from. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have been delegated Send-As or Send-On-Behalf permission for. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The subject of the email to create

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the email to create

parameters.name: to_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the recipients of the email

parameters.name: cc_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the CC recipients of the email.

parameters.name: bcc_recipients
parameters.description: The email addresses that will be the BCC recipients of the email.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The content type of the email body. Defaults to plain text.

tools.name: SharedMailboxCreateDraftReply
tools.description:
Create a reply or reply-all draft in a shared or delegated mailbox without sending it.

The draft is threaded to the original message and saved to the mailbox's
Drafts folder, so it can be reviewed, edited, and sent later. For a
reply-all, the original recipients (excluding the mailbox owner) are
populated automatically. Use cc_add to copy someone in on the draft,
including someone who was never on the thread, and cc_remove to take
somebody off the copied line; who the reply is addressed to is the thread's
own and reply_type decides it. This tool never sends the email.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to create the reply draft in. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email to create a reply draft for

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the reply draft

parameters.name: reply_type
parameters.description: Specify ReplyType.REPLY to draft a reply to only the sender, or ReplyType.REPLY_ALL to draft a reply to all recipients. Defaults to ReplyType.REPLY.

parameters.name: cc_add
parameters.description: Addresses to copy on the reply draft, in addition to whoever Outlook already copied. On a reply to all recipients Outlook copies the thread's other participants, and they stay copied — this only adds. Omit it to copy nobody new. Each address is copied once, and an address the draft already addresses is left addressed rather than also copied, so nobody receives the reply twice.

parameters.name: cc_remove
parameters.description: Addresses to take off the reply draft's copied line. Anyone Outlook copied and this does not name stays copied. Omit it to remove nobody; an address that is not on the copied line is ignored. An address the draft addresses cannot be taken off it — reply_type decides that line — so naming one is refused and no draft is kept.

parameters.name: bcc
parameters.description: Addresses to blind-copy on the reply draft. A blind-copied address receives the reply, once it is sent, without appearing on any other recipient's copy of it. Outlook never blind-copies anyone on a reply, so this is the whole line rather than a change to one. Omit it to blind-copy nobody.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: How body is read. Plain text reaches the recipient as the characters supplied, line breaks and angle brackets included; html reads body as markup, so tags in it render instead of being shown. Defaults to plain text. A reply draft is always stored as an HTML document because the quoted original is one, so this decides how body is read rather than what is stored.

body.value: Thank you for reaching out. We have reviewed your request and will get back to you with a resolution within 24 hours.

tools.name: SharedMailboxCreateMailFolder
tools.description:
Create a mail folder in a shared or delegated mailbox, to keep related messages together.

Creates the folder in the mailbox `owner_email` names, which is what a
request for a folder in a team mailbox, or in another person's, asks for.
The folder id it returns addresses that mailbox only. Safe to call for a folder that may
already exist: an existing folder of the same name under the same parent is
returned instead of a duplicate. A parent_folder that names no folder in
that mailbox creates nothing.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox to create the folder in. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide the exact mailbox email address.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name for the new folder, as it should read in Outlook. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the trimmed name is what gets created.

parameters.name: parent_folder
parameters.description: The folder to create this one inside, given as the word inbox or archive, or as a folder_id taken from a mail-folder listing of the owner_email mailbox. A display name or a path is refused: one display name can belong to several folders, and proving which one was meant costs a read of every folder in the mailbox, so the parent is named exactly or the request is declined. When omitted, the folder is created at the top level of that mailbox.

output.description: The folder with the message counts that belong to it, the folder that holds it, and whether this call is what created it.

tools.name: SharedMailboxGetEmail
tools.description:
Retrieve a single email from a shared or delegated mailbox by message ID.

Returns email metadata and body content. By default, the body is returned
as plain text (HTML tags stripped) and capped at 5000 characters. Use
body_offset to continue reading long emails:
body_total_characters reports how long the body is, and body_next_offset is
where the next call resumes.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to read from. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email message to retrieve.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: Format for the returned email body. PLAIN_TEXT strips HTML tags for clean reading. HTML returns the original markup. Defaults to PLAIN_TEXT.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Maximum number of characters to return from the email body. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the message without its body. The response always reports body_total_characters, so a body longer than the cap is read by calling again with body_offset set to the returned body_next_offset until body_has_more is false.

parameters.name: body_offset
parameters.description: Character offset to start reading the body from. Use this to continue reading a long email body that was previously capped. Defaults to 0 (start of body).

tools.name: SharedMailboxListEmailAttachments
tools.description: List attachment metadata for an email in a shared or delegated mailbox.

tools.name: SharedMailboxListEmails
tools.description:
List email messages in a shared or delegated mailbox.

Returns ordinary mail by default: Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and
Drafts are left out unless named in folders, folder_ids or conversation_id.
Each row reports the folder it came from in parent_folder_id.

Every filter narrows the same result set, so unread mail in one folder is a
single call.

Naming exactly one folder reads that folder itself, which is also the only
read a mailbox shared one folder at a time can serve. If a call that names
no folder, or several, is refused for lack of access to the whole mailbox,
repeat it naming one folder at a time.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: Email address of the mailbox to read, for example a team or resource mailbox.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Well-known folders to list mail from. Omit to read every folder except Deleted Items, Junk Email, Sent Items and Drafts. Naming folders replaces that default rather than adding to it. Combined with conversation_id, this narrows the thread to these folders. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: folder_ids
parameters.description: Ids of user-created folders to list mail from. Combined with any value given for folders. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Return only messages in this conversation, across every folder including Sent Items and Deleted Items. Naming folders or folder_ids alongside it narrows the thread to those folders, so leave both out to see all of it. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject match, as a value plus the operator to compare it with. Defaults to None (no subject filter).

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Sender email address match, as a value plus the operator to compare it with. Defaults to None (no sender filter).

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: True for read mail, False for unread. Defaults to None (both).

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: True for mail carrying attachments, False for mail without. Defaults to None (both).

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Return only mail at this importance level, and nothing else. Never use it to express an exclusion: setting it to normal to mean 'not low' drops every high-importance message. Use exclude_importance for that. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: exclude_importance
parameters.description: Return mail at every importance level except this one. Leave importance out alongside it: naming both narrows to a single level instead of excluding one. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: flag_status
parameters.description: Return only mail in this follow-up flag state. Defaults to None (any).

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Omit it, or leave it empty, for no lower bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Return only mail received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). The whole of that day is included. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no upper bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused, using Outlook's Focused Inbox split. Sender addresses are not inspected. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Property to sort results by. Defaults to received date.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to descending.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of messages to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same listing arguments alongside it: a cursor names a listing rather than a row number, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. Defaults to None (the first page).

output.description: The matching messages, and whether a further page exists.

tools.name: SharedMailboxListMailFolders
tools.description:
List mail folders in a shared or delegated mailbox.

Returns folder names, IDs, unread counts, and total item counts. A returned
folder ID is what scopes a mail listing to a user-created folder.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to read folders from. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: parent_folder_id
parameters.description: ID of a parent folder to list child folders of. When omitted, lists top-level mailbox folders.

parameters.name: include_hidden
parameters.description: Whether to include hidden folders in the response. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of folders to return. Max is 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed position to start from. Repeat the same arguments alongside it: every page is described by the call that asked for it, so a filter left out on the second page widens the second page. Defaults to 0 (the first result). Pass back the next_offset the response returns rather than adding limit yourself.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SharedMailboxMarkEmails
tools.description:
Set the read state or the follow-up flag on emails in a shared or delegated mailbox.

One call for a list of ids, a whole thread, or a search, reporting one
outcome per email. Select exactly one way. An email already in the state
asked for is a success that changed nothing, and a job needing more than 50
changes is refused whole rather than part-done.

A request to star, pin, flag or follow up on mail is this call; it never
moves the mail.

Needs Full Access to the mailbox; a folder-level share is refused.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox holding the emails, as its exact address. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Every id in this call -- of an email, of a folder -- belongs to this mailbox and resolves nowhere else.

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Whether the selected emails should end up read. Defaults to None (leave it as it is).

parameters.name: flag_status
parameters.description: What the follow-up flag should end up as. complete drops the start and due dates, which each row hands back. Defaults to None (leave it as it is); naming start_date or due_date alone sets flagged.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: When the follow-up begins: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS ending in Z or +HH:MM. A bare date means 08:00, and a time with no Z or offset is read, in this mailbox's timezone. Defaults to None (keep the current start; a new deadline with no start begins today).

parameters.name: due_date
parameters.description: The follow-up deadline, in the same formats as start_date. A bare date means 17:00 in this mailbox's timezone, not the signed-in user's. Records a deadline, not a reminder. Defaults to None (keep the current deadline).

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Narrow to emails currently in these folders: the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or a folder_id from a folder listing. Display names and paths are refused. A word also reaches whatever is filed under that folder. Naming folders replaces the selection's own scope, so name every folder to cover, including sentitems or drafts. Alongside message_ids, an email outside them comes back skipped. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: message_ids
parameters.description: The emails to act on, as the ids a listing, a search or an email read reported. At most 50 per request. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to select emails by, in Outlook's own search syntax, such as from:sara@contoso.com or wording from the subject. Write a phrase as the words alone. Deleted and junk mail are left out unless folders names them. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The thread to act on, as the conversation_id a listing or a search reported. Covers its mail wherever it sits; the mailbox's own sent replies and unsent drafts come back skipped unless folders names them. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Take the next set of a selection a previous call stopped short of, as the cursor it reported. Keep calling with the last cursor, beside the same selector and folders, until it comes back empty. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Report what the request would affect and change nothing, listing the ids, so a job too big for one call can be run in batches of them. Defaults to False.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SharedMailboxMoveEmails
tools.description:
Move a selection of emails into one folder in a shared or delegated mailbox.

Use this single call for a pile of emails instead of moving them one at a
time: it takes a list of ids, a whole conversation, or a search, and reports
one outcome per email.

Select the emails exactly one way. Naming none, or naming two, is refused
and moves nothing, as is a selection of more than 50 emails.

A conversation spans folders, so filing a thread moves the unsent drafts
and sent replies in it too unless folders narrows the selection. Run the
request with count_only first when that matters: it reports which folders
the mail would leave before anything moves.

Anything the caller got wrong -- the selection, an id, a folder that names
several folders or none -- is refused before the first email moves. After
that, an email Outlook refuses is reported as a failed row beside the ones
that moved rather than failing the whole request.

Filing into junk is not a reversible hide: Outlook permanently deletes mail
left in the Junk Email folder after 14 days, it does not report the sender
to Microsoft, and it does not train the junk filter. Tell the user that
before junking mail on their behalf.

Outlook does not record where an email came from, so putting mail back is a
move to the inbox like any other: name inbox as the destination, and name
the folder it is coming out of in folders so mail sitting elsewhere is left
alone.

Filing needs Full Access to the mailbox. A mailbox the signed-in user holds
one folder at a time instead -- a MAPI folder share -- is refused with that
said, because every selection here reads the mailbox above the shared
folder.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox holding the emails, as its exact address. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Every id in this call -- of an email, of a folder -- belongs to this mailbox and resolves nowhere else.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: The folder to move the selected emails into, as one of the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or as a folder_id from a folder listing of the mailbox named by owner_email. A display name or a path is refused: one display name can belong to several folders, and filing mail into the wrong one is not undoable, so the folder is named exactly or the request is declined. archive is this mailbox's own Archive folder, which is Outlook's One-Click Archive, not a separate Exchange Online archive mailbox. This never creates a folder.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Only move emails that are currently in these folders, each given as one of the words inbox, archive, junk or trash, or as a folder_id from a folder listing of the mailbox named by owner_email. Display names and paths are refused, for the same reason as destination. One of the four words also reaches whatever is filed underneath that folder; a folder_id means that folder alone, so to include what is filed underneath one, list its children and name them here too. Use it to file the part of a thread that is in the Inbox without moving the unsent drafts and sent replies in the same thread, and to put junked or deleted mail back in the inbox without disturbing mail that is already elsewhere. Alongside message_ids an email outside these folders is reported as skipped and left where it is; alongside query or conversation_id it is left out of the selection. Naming folders replaces the default exclusion of deleted and junk mail rather than adding to it, and costs one search per folder named. Defaults to None (the whole selection, wherever it sits).

parameters.name: message_ids
parameters.description: The emails to act on, as the ids a listing, a search or a message read of this same mailbox reported. At most 50 per request, and more than that is refused rather than trimmed. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to select emails by, in Outlook's own search syntax, such as from:sara@contoso.com or wording from the subject. Write a phrase as the words alone: double quotes around it are refused rather than searched for. Deleted and junk mail are left out unless folders names one of them. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The conversation to act on, as the conversation_id a listing, a search or a message read of this same mailbox reported. Selects every message in that thread, including ones in other folders such as unsent drafts and sent replies; name folders alongside it to act on only part of the thread. Defaults to None (select the emails another way).

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Report what the request would affect and change nothing: how many emails would move, which folders they would leave, and their ids. A search or a conversation holding more emails than one request moves is counted rather than refused, so a job too big to run in one call can be sized and then run in batches of those ids. Defaults to False (carry the request out).

output.description:
What one filing request selected, what it changed, and what it did not.

    items holds one row per selected message and is never paginated or
    truncated: the selection cap is the page. It is empty when count_only was
    set, because nothing was written to report. Each row's message_id is an id
    this mailbox accepts for that message, so a row can be chained straight
    into a read or a further move - with one limit named by id_shape: a legacy
    id, which is what a keyword search reports, stops resolving once the
    message has been filed somewhere else, so chain it before the next move
    rather than after. Every row also carries durable_message_id, which names
    the same message after this move whatever shape the selection was made
    with, and is the id to chain when the move has already happened.

    counts covers every row status. succeeded means the message was somewhere
    else and is now in the destination; already_there means it was there
    before this call and is a success rather than a change; skipped means the
    message was outside the folders the caller confined the move to, and it
    was left where it is; throttled means Outlook rate-limited
    that message and nothing was written for it; failed means Outlook refused
    it; not_attempted means the request ran out of time before reaching it;
    indeterminate means Outlook did not say, so read the message before
    retrying.

    complete is true only when every row is succeeded or already_there, and
    true on a count, which leaves nothing undone because it attempts nothing.

    preview is filled only when count_only was set. would_change counts the
    messages that would move, already_there those that are in the destination
    already, not_eligible those outside the folders the move was confined to,
    and classification_unknown those whose current folder could not be read. A
    count describes a selection the move itself would refuse for being over
    the cap rather than refusing to describe it, and says so in notes; the ids
    it would act on ride selection.message_ids so that refusal can be answered
    by moving them in cap-sized batches.

    moved_from aggregates the folders mail left, one entry per source folder. A
    count reports what would leave each folder, so a selection spanning Drafts
    or Sent Items is visible before anything moves.

    selection describes how the messages were chosen. mode is which selector
    was used - message_ids, conversation_id or query - and value is the
    conversation id or the search it was given, empty for a list of ids.
    count_is_exact is false
    when the number is a floor rather than a total, which is what a keyword
    search can honestly report; search_exhaustive says whether the scan reached
    the end of the matches; folders_searched names the folders the selection
    was narrowed to; folders_excluded names the folders a mailbox-wide keyword
    selection left out; duplicates_removed counts ids that named the same
    message twice and were acted on once.

    notes carries consequences of the move that the ledger does not show, such
    as what filing mail into the Junk Email folder does and does not do. They
    follow the folders the mail lands in and leaves, so reaching Junk Email by
    its display name carries the same warnings the junk shorthand does.

tools.name: SharedMailboxReplyToEmail
tools.description:
Reply to an email in a shared or delegated mailbox.

The reply is sent from the shared mailbox address, not the signed-in
user's personal address. Specify reply_type to reply only to the sender
or to all recipients. Use cc_add to copy someone in on the reply, including
someone who was never on the thread, and cc_remove to take somebody off the
copied line; who the reply is addressed to is the thread's own and reply_type
decides it.

The confirmation message names how many recipient addresses the reply went to
across To, Cc and Bcc, when Outlook reported the line it was addressed to.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to reply from. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the email to reply to

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body of the reply to the email

parameters.name: reply_type
parameters.description: Specify ReplyType.REPLY to reply only to the sender or ReplyType.REPLY_ALL to reply to all recipients. Defaults to ReplyType.REPLY.

parameters.name: cc_add
parameters.description: Addresses to copy on the reply, in addition to whoever Outlook already copied. On a reply to all recipients Outlook copies the thread's other participants, and they stay copied — this only adds. Omit it to copy nobody new. Each address is copied once, and an address the reply already addresses is left addressed rather than also copied, so nobody receives the reply twice.

parameters.name: cc_remove
parameters.description: Addresses to take off the reply's copied line. Anyone Outlook copied and this does not name stays copied. Omit it to remove nobody; an address that is not on the copied line is ignored. An address the reply addresses cannot be taken off it — reply_type decides that line — so naming one is refused and nothing is sent.

parameters.name: bcc
parameters.description: Addresses to blind-copy on the reply. A blind-copied address receives the reply without appearing on any other recipient's copy of it. Outlook never blind-copies anyone on a reply, so this is the whole line rather than a change to one. Omit it to blind-copy nobody.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: How body is read. Plain text reaches the recipient as the characters supplied, line breaks and angle brackets included; html reads body as markup, so tags in it render instead of being shown. Defaults to plain text. A reply is always stored as an HTML document because the quoted original is one, so this decides how body is read rather than what is stored.

body.value: Thank you for reaching out! We have reviewed your request and will get back to you with a resolution within 24 hours. Please let us know if you have any additional questions.

tools.name: SharedMailboxSaveDraftEmail
tools.description:
Save an email draft in a shared or delegated Outlook mailbox.

Supplying message_id revises that draft; omitting it creates a new one. Only the
fields supplied are written — anything left out keeps whatever the draft already
had. Nothing is ever sent.

Returns a DraftMessage. Its message_id identifies the saved draft and can be passed
straight back to this tool to make further changes to it.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox to save the draft in. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The draft to save the changes onto. Omit it to create a new draft instead. Any un-sent message works, including a reply or forward draft. The id of a draft saved earlier in this conversation is the message_id this tool returned; the id of a draft that already existed comes from listing the mailbox's Drafts folder.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The subject to set. Omit it to leave the current subject unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The body to set. Omit it to leave the current body unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.

parameters.name: to_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of To recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the To line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every To recipient.

parameters.name: cc_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of Cc recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the Cc line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every Cc recipient.

parameters.name: bcc_recipients
parameters.description: The complete list of Bcc recipients, replacing whatever the draft currently carries: any address left out of this list is removed from the draft, so include the ones to keep as well as the ones to add. Read the draft first when the current list is not already known. Omit it to leave the Bcc line untouched; pass an empty list to remove every Bcc recipient.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The content type of body. Has no effect unless body is supplied. Omit it to keep whatever content type the draft already carries when revising one, or to write plain text on a new draft.

tools.name: SharedMailboxSearchEmails
tools.description:
Search emails in a shared or delegated mailbox.

Combines full-text keyword search with structured filters for sender,
read status, attachments, importance, and more. All provided parameters
are combined with AND.

At least one search criterion is required. folder, only_focused,
include_body and limit narrow or page a result set rather than build one,
so they are not enough on their own.

Junk Email and Deleted Items are left out unless `folder` names one of them;
sent mail and drafts stay searchable. Rows carry a 255-character body preview
unless include_body is set.

Results come back in the search index's own order and cannot be re-sorted.

Outlook's search index answers one query with at most 1,000 messages, so a
walk that runs out of pages has reached the end of what the index serves
rather than the end of the mailbox. The folders left out and the Focused
split are applied to those 1,000 after they are chosen, so a broad term
matching a lot of junk can come back with few rows, or none, while matching
mail exists. A narrower term reaches it; a smaller limit does not.

.. note::
   Search results may use a different Graph ID shape than list/get
   results. Use returned message IDs directly for message retrieval and
   ``conversation_id`` for deduplication across result sets.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address to search. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description: Words or phrases to search for across email subject, body, and sender fields. All terms must match (AND operator). Defaults to None.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Narrow the hunt to the subject line. Matched as words within the subject rather than as the whole line. Defaults to None (no subject narrowing).

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Filter by sender email address, display name, or alias. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Filter by To-recipient email address or display name. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: attachment_name
parameters.description: Filter by attachment filename. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: has_attachments
parameters.description: Filter for emails with or without attachments. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Filter by email importance level. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: is_read
parameters.description: Filter by read status. True for read emails, False for unread. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by email category name. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: received_after
parameters.description: Filter for emails received on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no lower bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: received_before
parameters.description: Filter for emails received on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Dates are interpreted in UTC. Omit it, or leave it empty, for no upper bound. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Search a single folder instead of the whole mailbox. Omit to search everywhere except Junk Email and Deleted Items. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: only_focused
parameters.description: Return only mail the mailbox itself classified as Focused. Sender addresses are not inspected. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: include_body
parameters.description: Return each message's full body. Defaults to False, which returns a preview of at most 255 characters per row.

parameters.name: max_body_characters
parameters.description: Cap on body characters per row when include_body is True. Defaults to 5000; 0 returns the row without a body. Ignored when include_body is False. A row cut at the cap is marked body_truncated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Values above 25 are clamped to 25 and the response reports limit_clamped_to_max; values below 1 are raised to 1. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Position of a further page, copied from a previous response's cursor. Repeat the same search arguments alongside it, only_focused included: a cursor names a search rather than a position in a result set, and one handed back beside different arguments is refused. Defaults to None (the first page).

tools.name: SharedMailboxSendDraftEmail
tools.description:
Send an existing draft email from a shared or delegated mailbox.

This tool can send any un-sent email in the shared mailbox:
    - draft
    - reply-draft
    - reply-all draft
    - forward draft

Returns the message's ``message_id`` and ``conversation_id`` so callers
can chain follow-ups (e.g. reply to the message they just sent) without
searching Sent Items.

parameters.name: owner_email
parameters.description: The mailbox address that owns the draft. Can be a team or shared mailbox, or a specific person's mailbox you have delegate access to. Provide as a Microsoft Graph UPN (local-part@verified-domain).

parameters.name: message_id
parameters.description: The ID of the draft email to send

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description:
Get the signed-in user's profile and the mailbox this toolkit acts on.

Returns the user's name, email, tenant and other profile details, plus the mailbox
the toolkit reads mail from. mailbox_timezone identifies the mailbox's configured
time zone or the fallback identified by mailbox_timezone_source. received_date_time
remains in UTC; received_date_time_local contains its local representation when
available.

mailbox_timezone may be a Windows name such as "Eastern Standard Time" rather than an
IANA identifier - that names a zone observing daylight saving, not a fixed offset.
mailbox_timezone_source says where that zone came from: "mailbox" and "mailbox_utc"
mean the mailbox itself names the zone, whereas "default_not_configured" (the mailbox
names none) and "default_unreadable" (the setting could not be read) mean UTC is a
fallback this toolkit applied, not a zone the mailbox is set to. On either fallback,
do not tell the user their mailbox is configured for that zone.

output.description: The signed-in user's profile, the mailbox this toolkit acts on, and its time zone.

documentationChunks.content:
<Callout type="warning">
  The Microsoft Outlook Mail MCP server requires a Microsoft work or school account.
  Personal Microsoft accounts, such as `@outlook.com` and `@hotmail.com`, are
  not supported. See the [Microsoft auth
  provider](/references/auth-providers/microsoft) reference for details.
</Callout>

summary:
The **MicrosoftOutlookMail** toolkit connects Arcade to Microsoft Outlook Mail via Microsoft Graph, enabling LLM agents to read, compose, send, organize, and search email in both personal and shared/delegated mailboxes.

## Capabilities

- **Read & search mail** — Retrieve individual messages (with pagination for long bodies), list messages by folder/thread/filter, search by keyword and structured criteria across the full mailbox, and inspect attachment metadata.
- **Compose & send** — Create and immediately send new emails; reply (sender-only or reply-all) and forward existing messages, with control over To/Cc/Bcc and inline Cc additions or removals.
- **Draft management** — Save new drafts or revise existing ones, create reply/reply-all and forward drafts, then send any draft when ready — all without triggering a send prematurely.
- **Mail organization** — Move batches of messages (by ID list, thread, or search result) into any folder, mark messages read/unread or flagged, and create mail folders and subfolders.
- **Shared & delegated mailboxes** — A full parallel set of tools covers team inboxes (e.g. `sales@`, `support@`) and delegated executive mailboxes: list, search, read, compose, reply, forward, draft, send, move, mark, create folders, and check mailbox accessibility.
- **Identity & timezone** — Resolve the signed-in user's profile, primary mailbox address, tenant, and configured mailbox timezone (including fallback detection).

## OAuth

This toolkit uses **OAuth 2.0** via the **Microsoft** provider. See the [Arcade Microsoft auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/microsoft) for configuration details including required scopes.
